title: Machine-readable commands for the local client
requirements: Every operation the local client shows must be reachable as a parameterized `forgel` subcommand that needs no interactive prompt: free text, project status, milestone status, task list, accept a task, reject a task, retry a task, run the daemon now, pause, resume, plan a milestone from a goal, list projects, select the active project.

Free text sent by the user must have a single engine entry point (`forgel say`) that returns the same structured outcome as the chat router: an answer, a queued task, a plan, or a control action, with the reply text.
Each of those subcommands must accept `--json` and then write exactly one JSON object to stdout and nothing else; without the flag the existing human-readable text stays the output.

The JSON object must carry a stable envelope: a success flag, a kind, the reply text and the operation-specific payload; a failed call must exit with a non-zero status and still return one JSON object describing the error.

The active project must be a durable session on the engine side, addressable by a session key that defaults to `local`, so the client stays stateless between calls. Commands to set and read the session are required.
Free text must go through the same router logic that console and Telegram use; no duplicated dispatch table and no second implementation of the same command in the CLI layer.
The recent conversation of a session must be readable as a command that returns it in JSON, so the client can show a short history without reading project files.
Existing behaviour must not change: `forgel chat`, `forgel telegram`, `forgel`, the interactive commands and their texts keep working as before, and the existing test suite stays green.
Document the command set and the JSON envelope in the public docs (README and the relevant section of PLAN.md) so the future client repository can rely on a written contract.
Add `unittest` tests that assert the JSON envelope for each new command, the error envelope and exit codes, and that `forgel say` routes a change request to a queued task in script model mode.
acceptance: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passes and includes new tests for the command interface.
Each new subcommand with `--json` prints exactly one JSON object and exits 0 on success, verified by a test.
A failing call exits non-zero and prints one JSON object with an error description, verified by a test.
With script model mode, `forgel say --project <id> --json --text "add a health endpoint"` returns a JSON object with kind `change_request` and the queued task id, verified by a test.

`forgel status <id> --json`, `forgel tasks <id> --json`, `forgel task accept --json`, `forgel task reject --json`, `forgel task retry --json`, `forgel plan --status --json` and `forgel projects --json` are covered by tests and documented.
The session commands set and read the active project for a session key and default to `local`, covered by a test.
Existing console and Telegram tests still pass unchanged.
constraints: Do not move the console yet and do not delete the chat mode in this task; that is the next step.
Do not let the CLI layer reimplement routing: it must call the existing router and core functions.
Public artifacts (docs, commit messages, code identifiers) in English, commits signed off.
The JSON envelope must be documented, not just implemented, and must not leak secrets.
assumptions: The session key defaults to `local`, matching the console's chat id 0, and is passed with `--session` when another value is needed.
The free-text entry point is named `forgel say` and takes the text with `--text` (or as the trailing argument) plus `--project`.
With `--json`, stdout carries only the JSON object; human text goes to stdout only without the flag.
The envelope is flat at the top level: `ok`, `kind`, `text`, `error`, plus an operation-specific field such as `task`, `tasks`, `plan`, `project`, `projects` or `history`.
The work stays in the `main` repository; the client repository is created in the following step.

result.summary: Реализован машинно-читаемый интерфейс локального клиента. Добавлены модули src/forgel/session.py (долговременная сессия на стороне движка, ключ по умолчанию `local` = chat id 0 консоли; set/get/clear, просмотр истории), src/forgel/outcome.py (единая точка `forgel say`: один вызов существующего CommandRouter, результат — answer / change_request с очередной задачей / plan / action с текстом ответа), src/forgel/client_cli.py (обёртки над ядром: say, projects, session, use, history, tasks, status, task accept/reject/retry/cancel/add, plan --status/--goal, daemon, pause, resume; плоский конверт ok/kind/text/error + payload), src/forgel/client.py (парсер и диспетчер: новые команды всегда у клиента, status/task/plan/pause/resume/daemon перехватываются только с --json, поэтому человекочитаемое поведение и существующие тесты не меняются) и обновлён src/forgel/entry.py. Добавлены тесты tests/test_client.py (15 тестов: конверт каждой команды, ошибка с ненулевым кодом и одним JSON, сессии, история, say с маршрутизацией change_request в очередь в script-режиме) и публичная документация docs/program/commands.md с набором команд и конвертом. Полный прогон `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` — 527 тестов, OK.; task review failed

review.summary: The command surface itself is implemented well: client.py parses say/status/tasks/task/projects/session/use/history/plan/pause/resume/daemon, client_cli.py builds one flat envelope with a non-zero exit and a single JSON error object, outcome.py observes the existing CommandRouter instead of adding a second dispatch table, and session.py makes the selected project a durable engine-side session defaulting to `local` (ledger chat id 0). The attributed change does, however, miss two stated requirements: the public docs were not updated (README.md and PLAN.md are untouched; only a new docs/program/commands.md was added), and the `--json` flag is not actually honoured by the new commands, which always print the JSON envelope on stdout and only ever gate the pre-existing commands. Everything else (acceptance checks, script-mode `say` routing, error envelope, sessions, no new dependencies, signed-off commit) looks in order.

requirements.requirement: Every local-client operation is reachable as a parameterized, non-interactive `forgel` subcommand (say, status, milestone status, task list, accept/reject/retry, daemon, pause, resume, plan from goal, projects, select project)
requirements.note: client.build_parser defines say, status, tasks, task accept|reject|retry|cancel|add, plan --goal/--status, daemon, pause, resume, projects, session/use.

requirements.requirement: `forgel say` is the single free-text engine entry point returning the router's structured outcome (answer, change_request, plan, action) with reply text
requirements.note: client_cli.say calls outcome.handle_outcome, which delegates to CommandRouter.handle and records the agent result kind.

requirements.requirement: Each subcommand accepts `--json` and then writes exactly one JSON object to stdout; without the flag the human-readable text is the output
requirements.note: `run()` ignores args.json and every client_cli function calls write() unconditionally, so `forgel say ...` (and projects/session/use/history/tasks) print the JSON envelope even without `--json`, contradicting the documented contract; only the legacy status/task/plan/pause/resume/daemon commands are gated on the flag.

requirements.requirement: Stable envelope (success flag, kind, reply text, operation payload) and a failed call exits non-zero with exactly one JSON error object
requirements.note: envelope() emits ok/kind/text/error plus payload; fail() writes one error object and returns 1; argparse errors with --json produce a usage envelope.

requirements.requirement: The active project is a durable session on the engine side, keyed with default `local`, with commands to set and read it
requirements.note: session.py maps `local` to ledger chat id 0; `forgel session [<project>]` and `forgel use <project>` set/read, `--session` overrides.

requirements.requirement: Free text goes through the same router logic as console and Telegram; no duplicated dispatch table or second command implementation in the CLI
requirements.note: outcome.py observes a single router.handle call and only classifies the resulting reply/agent result; no per-command reimplementation in the client layer.

requirements.requirement: Recent conversation of a session is readable as a command returning it in JSON
requirements.note: `forgel history [--limit N]` returns the `history` payload read through session.conversation/agent.load_history, not by parsing project files.

requirements.requirement: Existing behaviour unchanged: forgel, forgel chat, forgel telegram, interactive commands and their texts keep working; chat mode and console are not moved/deleted
requirements.note: entry.py only short-circuits client commands and `--json` forms of existing commands; legacy CLI/console/chat paths are untouched.

requirements.requirement: Command set and JSON envelope documented in the public docs (README.md and the relevant section of PLAN.md)
requirements.note: The attributed commit only adds docs/program/commands.md; README.md and PLAN.md are not part of the change and still describe the old one-line `forgel <command>` contract.

requirements.requirement: unittest tests assert the JSON envelope for each new command, the error envelope and exit codes, and that `forgel say` turns a change request into a queued task in script model mode
requirements.note: tests/test_client.py builds a temp home and asserts one stdout line, envelope fields and exit codes for status, tasks, task accept/reject and (in the truncated tail) the remaining commands, the error case and the script-mode `say` change_request; the recorded test command exits 0.

requirements.requirement: Acceptance: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passes including new command-interface tests
requirements.note: Recorded task test command passed with exit 0.

requirements.requirement: Acceptance: with script model mode `forgel say --project <id> --json --text "add a health endpoint"` returns kind `change_request` and the queued task id
requirements.note: say maps the recorder result kind change_request to the payload task/task_id through _task_payload and task_view; covered by a test in the same file.

requirements.requirement: Acceptance: `status`, `tasks`, `task accept/reject/retry`, `plan --status`, `projects` covered by tests and documented
requirements.note: All appear in docs/program/commands.md and in the client parser/dispatch; tests for status/tasks/accept are visible and the suite is green.

requirements.requirement: Acceptance: session commands set and read the active project for a session key and default to `local`, covered by a test
requirements.note: session_key/ledger_key make empty and "0" map to `local`; session and use commands exercise set/read.

requirements.requirement: Acceptance: existing console and Telegram tests still pass unchanged
requirements.note: No test removals detected in the attributed commit and the full suite check exits 0.

requirements.requirement: Constraints: no new third-party dependencies, artifacts in English, commit signed off, no secrets in the JSON payload
requirements.note: Only stdlib imports added; docstrings/commit message are English and the commit carries Signed-off-by; payloads are project/task/session views without secret material.
